clue.text: Prudent means of raising money — one kept in reserve!

indicators.note: something kept in a store sits inside it, so these letters go inside the word for reserve

parts.note: to reserve or preserve something is to conserve it
VAT, value added tax, is a government's way of raising revenue
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cautious fundraising scheme that keeps one item back in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'means of raising money' sound like a savings plan; it is simply a tax, and 'kept in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cautious, careful approach avoids risk, which is what both words describe.

clue.text: Bag up chops made from nuts

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a baglike pouch
to chop wood is to hew it

explanation.surface: A bag of chopped food made from nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the bag word from the bottom; 'chops' looks like a noun (cuts of meat) but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney-shaped edible kernels from a tropical tree.

clue.text: Never affected by strong spirit

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has never been affected by strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges NEVER. 'spirit' suggests alcohol but means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or boldness is a strong spirit.

clue.text: No longer stress the spread

parts.note: EX means former, no longer so
stress is tension

explanation.surface: Someone stops worrying about the spread of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreading out or enlargement is an extension.

clue.text: Star is upset — time not on her side?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: an age is a period of time
V is short for versus, against or not on one's side

explanation.surface: A film star is upset because time is against her as she ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AGEV, giving the star's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: With credit a thing of the past, only just keep going

parts.note: buying on tick is informal British for buying on credit
something over is finished and in the past

explanation.surface: With credit gone, a business can only just stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine idling runs slowly without doing work, just keeping going.

clue.text: See a hat needs binding

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A hat needs a ribbon binding round it.
explanation.walkthrough: V for vide (see) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid contract is legally binding.

clue.text: Quietly made haste to phone about dinner

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
to make haste is to run
to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to ring round about a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Prandial means relating to a meal, especially dinner.

clue.text: Fish for example raised to order

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, bottom to top

explanation.surface: Fish such as these were bred to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to command or instruct them.

clue.text: Tigers' act is unpredictable, as planned

indicators.note: something unpredictable will not stay in a fixed order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A circus tiger act cannot be predicted, though it is meant to be choreographed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unpredictable' rearranges TIGERSACT; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done according to a deliberate scheme or plan is strategic.

clue.text: Many a bow is made of such wood

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
an arch is a bow-shaped curve

explanation.surface: An observation that archery bows are often carved from a particular timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests archery; the bow is an arch shape and 'Many' gives the Roman L.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is a common wood.

clue.text: How players bow out

parts.note: the stage direction telling actors to leave together, from the Latin for 'they go out'

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction printed in scripts when several actors leave the stage.

clue.text: Putting pounds on, finished right — capital fellow!

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling
taken as written
something finished is done

explanation.surface: Someone who has gained weight and done the right thing is hailed as a splendid chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital fellow' sounds like old-fashioned praise but means a man from the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of the British capital city is known by this name.

clue.text: A race calling for tremendous effort

definitions.meaning: a breed or stock of animals or plants
a heavy exertion that taxes body or mind

explanation.surface: A running race that demands an enormous effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not a contest here but a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed or lineage is one sense; overexertion or heavy stress is the other.

clue.text: Note the nurse in charge is one who won't yield an inch

definitions.text: one who won't yield an inch

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
in British hospitals a sister is the senior nurse of a ward

explanation.surface: A ward sister is noted as never giving an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sister is the British title for a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes and holds out without giving way.

clue.text: This bird will have to look around a bit

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, so A SNIP sits inside the word for look

parts.note: to look is to see
a snip is a small piece cut off

explanation.surface: A bird needs to look about it for a scrap of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; 'a bit' is a small cutting, not a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal wading bird, a kind of snipe found by the shore.

clue.text: Rudeness about the head is a danger signal

indicators.note: one word is placed about the other, so TOP goes inside SLIGHT

parts.note: a slight is a snub or rude discourtesy
top means head, the uppermost part

explanation.surface: Rudeness aimed at the boss is a warning sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Rudeness' is the outer word and 'the head' the inner one.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic light that warns drivers to halt.

clue.text: A bloomer bad lads hope to make!

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Badly behaved lads hope to make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges LADSHOPE. 'bloomer' looks like a gaffe but is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-family plant with spikes of flowers, so something that blooms.

clue.text: He's only too pleased to give one a light

definitions.text: He's only too pleased to give one a light

parts.words: He's only too pleased to give one a light
parts.note: reads like a friendly smoker offering a match, but describes someone who loves setting fires

explanation.definitionFit: A person who deliberately starts fires would happily set someone's property ablaze.

clue.text: The outlook for coppers interrupting a party

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, so P goes inside the letters of a party

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
P stands for pence, copper coins

explanation.surface: The prospects for police officers who barge into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means pennies, P. 'interrupting' puts P inside ASECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A view facing a particular way is an aspect.

clue.text: A model gets work, even if a shapeless lump

parts.note: a doll is a small model of a person
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A fashion model lands a job even though she is rather lumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is an unformed blob of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: Daring to read the newspapers without a pained expression

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the press wraps round the cry

parts.note: the press means newspapers
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Bravely reading the papers without wincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the newspapers wrap round the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is skill or bravery in combat.

clue.text: Jumble? It's cheap rubbish!

indicators.note: used like 'trash' as a verb, so these letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A jumble sale item is dismissed as worthless trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' rearranges ITSCHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley or hotchpotch of borrowed styles and pieces.

clue.text: Children causing controversy?

explanation.surface: Are children causing an argument?
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring, as in legal wills, and a point in dispute.

clue.text: A spinner for life, such is fate

definitions.text: A spinner for life, such is fate

parts.words: A spinner for life, such is fate
parts.note: in Greek myth one of the three Fates spins the thread of each human life

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology she is the Fate who spins the thread of every human life.

clue.text: Dance to beat with animation

parts.note: to tan is to beat or thrash
go is energy or animation

explanation.surface: Dancing to a beat with plenty of liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: To speak indistinctly is considered an affront

definitions.meaning: an insult or slight on someone

explanation.surface: Mumbling is taken as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbling words together, and an insulting remark that slights someone.

clue.text: Minor county finishing second in game

indicators.note: the second piece comes at the finish, after the county

parts.note: Ches. is the short form of Cheshire, which plays in cricket's Minor Counties Championship

explanation.surface: A minor-county cricket side ends up runner-up in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county; in cricket it is a 'minor county', outside the first-class game. 'finishing' puts S after CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game of strategy for two players.

clue.text: Coach-building industry

explanation.surface: A firm that builds coaches, the coach-building trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as coach-building industry; split it into a stagecoach and hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic stagecoach in one sense; steady, conscientious effort in the other.

clue.text: Notices cold stare — in a perplexed state

indicators.note: letters in a confused or perplexed state are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Someone gives a frosty glare at public notices while baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perplexed state' rearranges COLDSTAREINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal announcements or statements made publicly are declarations.
